title: Cradle
text: The world of Cradle is mysterious. It invites you with little handholding to try and make sense of it all. That there is some powerful mystery to be solved or some curious insight to he discovered. The first hour or so is a slow discovery of trying to figure out the history of this world as well as gradually repairing the strange robot in your hut. This part was rather fascinating and curious. However quite a few things mar this game. The little handholding can sometimes be too little. Yes it will always tell you what your current objective is, but sometimes it is unclear at how to accomplish it. Sometimes you need to find one particular item that can be difficult to locate. I certainly had one time accidentally knock the critical item I needed off a table into some corner of the room before I had realized that it was a critical item 30 minutes later. I had to use a guide a few times, especially one with pictures in order to know exactly what things such as a “Synchronizer” looked like. Eventually you get playing these simple games in a nearby amusement park. I am not sure how I feel about them, as they seem tonally different than the rest of the more interesting part of the game. Although they do provide a gameplay break from the exploration and story. But the worst part of this game is how it seems to abruptly end and its ending. While I understand what it is showing me in the ending, it is very unclear how/why this is happening. It felt like there was a number of things hinted in the background or dialog that was left unexplored. Ultimately, despite the interesting and promising beginning, I left feeling disappointed.

text: Don't let the pictures fool you, it may look like beautiful open world but sandbox game this is not. The really nice scenery ends  just up the hill where the character "blacks out". It's not like they couldn't have made it more open, its just not that kind of a game. Instead this is a point and click adventure centered around the idea of waking up inside a tent with amneisa next to a non-functional android and being required to piece together your memories and her body by solving puzzles, riddles and mini-games. Whether or not you like this game will depend strongly on whether or not you can appreciate story driven "investigating" and first-person puzzle games, I personally was able to get into both and really enjoyed this game. The story is really where this game shines, I love cyberpunk, psychological mystery type stuff and this story really covers a lot of ground. The only downside I find is that the ending feels .. unfinished. Yea, its one of "those" .. where its supposed to have you come up with the answers yourself but instead looks like they ran out of time and had to ship the game without an ending. However, the journey, the story and the adventuring and the puzzling were all enjoyable for me and I recommend this game to anyone who likes point-and-click adventure games. Just make sure you really know what this game is about before trying it.

title: Cradle

Where the game struggles is in its puzzles and story telling/ending. This is a game where you need to scour every inch of the game world to fully understand the game. text: This review is a recommendation with a 20-foot-tall BUT attached...  Absolutely gorgeous game, first of all.  The location is wonderfully realized and makes you feel like you really are in the middle of nowhere.  The area feels so big I never wanted to just go in one direction to see how big.  The whole world is scattered with tons of things to read.  It was cool that the main character was not a generic white guy, and the other main character was a lady.  The game very gently nudges you in a direction as to what your next objective is, so it never felt like it was hand-holding. BUT, all of this comes at a price...  The objectives of the game are so vague, it can be really hard to even know what the hell is going on.  "Find a red thing to do something with".  WTF am I supposed to do with that??  The game is built on what feels like a very thought out world that is not explored in the slighest.  The only other character is a robot with a wacky nose.  It's never explained why...for either part.  The ending is super abrupt and is barely explained at all.  Lastly, the game is chocked full of this horrific box puzzle game that is both not fun and very uncharacteristic.  You can however skip these games after you lose for the first time. P's & C's: + Beautiful + Streams wonderfully + Good writing + Lots of intractables + Doesn't hold your hand + Can skip the box portions - Ending is abrupt and unsatisfying - World not very well explored - Doesn't hold your hand...barely even gestures in a direction ---- Box puzzle that really seemed tacked on and almost made me stop playing (until I found out you could skip it) tl;dr: While I wouldn't recommend playing this game, it was competent enough to warrant not giving it a thumbs down. very-confused / 10, would try next game...

title: Cradle
text: Far too short, pretty poor performance and horrible cube throwing mini games. These 3 things completely spoil the game, which does have some pretty cool features/aspects. The visuals are overall pretty great, from the scenery to the robot(s) and their brilliant eyes. The story and voices are pretty good, some good puzzles too.  Framerate reugularly dips well below comfortable levels on a pretty decent rig (8 core cpu @ 5ghz, 16Gb DDR2400, 512Gb SSD, MSI GTX 980). Entire game took 4 hours for me to complete from start to finish and could easily be finished quicker, feels like the beggining of a game that was cut majorly short and had a slap-dash ending thrown in. The cube throwing mini games are atrocious! (3 or 4 in the game). Every one the same just with different colours and every one as bad as the last. After the first one you will find yourself simply falling into the water and jumping up and down, just to speed up the process of failing and then being offered the "skip mini game" option. Its a massive shame as i instantly fell in love with this game when i first seen it about a year ago, it hinted at a lot more of an open world exploration puzzle game when in reality you get a yurt(tent) and a very small abandoned fairground with a couple of hundred meters worth of empty grasslands in between. Cannot reccomend this at its current price, feels like an unfinished game that had completely "out of character" block throwing mini games to replace any meaningful exploration/puzzles. Might be worth checking out if you see it on sale at 60% off or more.

title: Cradle
text: Buy it cheap. Cheaper than the 8 bucks I spent. This is a game that raises far more questions than it answers, both in terms of its story as well as its design. Why is the map so vast yet all of the play area relatively constricted? Why does the ending come long before you understand what's happening? Why does the game tantalize you with the suggestion of a vast, intricate world, but never show it to you? Why are the block minigames so awful? The only explanation is that this was a game made on a budget, and that the creators cut all the corners they could to produce a barely viable product. Ultimately, Cradle is a game of wasted potential. I recommend it only to novelty seekers because it had vision, not because it is a good game. Everyone else will lose nothing by passing it up.

title: Crystals of Time
text: At first I thought this game was excellent. It had a great atmosphere and the music is truly lovely - melancholic but modern. However, the game fast gets repetive, falling into the lazy traps that many hidden object games do. The good points: 1. The music, as  I've said before is lovely. It fits nicely with the atmosphere and although it's not that varied it doesn't prove distracting, it adds to the experience. 2. Many of the mini puzzles are interesting and provide a bit of a challenge and variety. 3. The first 30 mins or so of gameplay are excellent, the diary gives you hints as to what you need to do and you don't mind skipping between locations to complete tasks/find objects. The bad points: 1. In order to solve many 'puzzles' you need to collect objects to complete an item. Often these objects are hidden in completely non-sensical locations meaning that you have to trawl through all the possible locations of hidden object scenes. This could be so much better if you thought 'Ah, I need a pipe, I think I'll try the storeroom' rather than 'Ah, I need something to fix this damn boat and the diary is giving me no clue, I'll try every location until I happen to stumble across the correct hidden object scene - one of the master bedrooms'. 2. In order to fix these 'puzzles' as I've said above, you have no real clue what you need to collect - there are no prompts - and so this undermines the puzzle element and just makes it a grind. 3. The diary soon becomes of no use whatsoever. The 'clues' you pick up don't really help and there are no prompts. 4. It feels very much like the game had a great germ of an idea but then didn't have the time to finish it. Overall a disappointing experience.

title: Crystals of Time
text: A very poor HOG game with little to no redeeming factors. Buy at your own risk. There is very little good to say about Crystals of Time. The soundtrack is pretty nice, but extremely limited, often stopping for minutes of a time leaving you in silence. The story is pretty much non-existent and the characters uninteresting. The worst part is the gameplay and the presentation however as the game is littered with horrible design decisions. The area is very open with many rooms to explore and return to. Unfortunately, the areas that need items are often very vague as to what is needed (“I should find the missing item first.” is the games favorite line… instead of giving some kind of hint what I’m actually trying to do there) and HOG item zones will activate with little rhyme or reason. For example there is a greenhouse which when you first visit does not have a HOG zone… but one activates later without giving you a single indication or reason to return to the greenhouse. Thus, you are forced to use hints or to go through every single room each time you are missing an item. As moving around in the game is very slow (the minimap can only take you to a few select locations) and the locations are very uninteresting to explore the game pretty much forces you to use hints a lot. The minigames and HOG sections themselves are uninspired. The items you search for are randomized and when you return to search the same area you often have to look for the same items again (even items that you previously took and used). Many objects are badly sized, coloured strangely, sometimes wrongly named and there is very low sensitivity to your clicks, e.g. you have to click very precisely and sometimes that is not enough. I once clicked 5 times on a chain and it simply refused to work making me believe it was the wrong item. It wasn’t. The time travelling gem that changes the scenes is nice… I guess. However, very little is done with it in the sections I played (I only found the first crystal before I finally decided this game was not worth playing). Only means you have to keep an eye on the crystal to see if you can change the time in a room. Anyway, I bought the game for about 1 Euro and still feel a bit cheated. Avoid.

That aside, gameplay is very simple and the mini-games are easy. The artwork is nice and the music adds to the mood of mystery. So it's not all bad, but definitely something you want to buy on sale, if at all.

title: Cubicle Quest
text: What an ingenious game! Start as a young adult with debts up the yin-yang and a low paying job. But you can change all that by leveling and destroying those horrible debt monsters. (Man, I wish you could do that in real life). Cubicle Quest has many unique aspects. You begin as the ruler of your own kingdom. The Debt Army is outside your castle and threatening to destroy everything so you've got your work cut out for you. As I've already stated, you begin with a low paying job and everytime you sleep in your bed in the castle, a month advances and you receive your salary - minus many expenses. Rent, food, utilities, entertainment, etc. - all these things eat away your money. However, in the basement of your castle, all these expenses are manifested as monsters that you can defeat to either eliminate or lower their cost. To the north of your castle is the Dungeon of Work where you can get a promotion (which means more money each month!), IF you can defeat the boss. Unfortunately, your main character, Bob, is kind of a doofus and as soon as he begins to earn more money, he begins spending more. Meaning more monsters to defeat in your castle basement. There are plenty of places where you can level up. There are also many different people who will join you on your quest - you just have to go out there and find them. You can have 4 active party members. Bob is always one so, most of the time, you can choose the other 3 based on your preferences. Luckily, the party members who aren't "active" still receive half of the experience the normal party gets after each fight. Battles are also unique in the fact that instead of having elements like fire, water, earth, and air, you're working with personal skills, human skills, work skills, and peace skills. Some enemies obviously fit into one of these categories but mostly you'll have to experiment. When you use a skill, you will see in big letters "Resist" or "Weak" (or nothing) on the monster you cast it on so try everything. At the end of a battle you receive experience and BP points. Equip books on your party that boost stats. I began with the History Book on everyone since that increases experience gained. Each book has a certain number (100 - 250). Fill up those books with BP points and you can unequip the book but continue to get the benefit from it! You don't receive gold from enemies - money only comes from your income or..... there's a little trick to getting rich. You can find lots of neat facts in many helpful guides found on Steam. Equipment in Cubicle Quest is also a bit different. Instead of equipping weapons and armor, you equip goals, communities, and virtues. Many of these things are strong against certain "elements" so if you're getting whooped in a dungeon, try equipment that protects against different things. Equipment with the highest stats aren't always the best choice. There's so much to explore and experiment with in this game - it's just a ton of fun. Dialog is usually clever and humorous as well. You can see how many hours I put into this and I loved every minute. Well, maybe not the times I was grinding for levels but you don't really have to do that often. I just like to be op. :p Now I'll list places of interest in the game and what my party was when I beat the "bonus" last boss. There are many secret areas and tons more open up after beating the game the first time. So here goes: Castle Sanity: Your very own castle. There are 2 basements - one with expense monsters and one that explains different aspects of the game. So both are very important! When you find a roommate to help with rent, they'll begin chilling in your castle. If you get married, your wife will also move here. And this is the place where you can deploy troops against the Debt Army (use your salary to lower your debts) and also advance months. Port Nostalgia: This is where Mom and Pop kingdom is. You can rest in an inn here for 200g which is something I did often to keep months from advancing. (I wanted to pay off my debts without getting super old - you DO age in Cubicle Quest). Societyville: Most of the shops are here. There's a library - explore that first to get some free books to equip on your party members and then buy the rest (the ones you're interested in). Get those History books equipped pronto! Societyville is also where you'll meet Jacob who will craft things for you - for free! You just need to find the items he requires. Some you can buy and others drop off certain monsters. Tower of Self-Improvement: Multiple floors - each containing a dungeon with treasures and bosses. Dungeon of Work: Where you go to get promoted and increase your monthly salary. Be prepared - it won't be easy! Financial Mine: Complete the left side of the dungeon to gain access to a bank account. Defeat the right side to open Investment options. There are many other places to find. I'll let you do the exploring. By the final end of the game, I managed to pay off all my debts, buy a house and a car, get married, ..... and I was finally able to pay off my mortgage at age 47. My wife helped. There are quite a few marriage options but some girls will add expenses to you. Others, like my choice, will chip in with the bills. And here's my final party: Bob: Level 83 (weapon) Goal: A Meaningful Life (armor) Community: Friendships Renewed (armor) Virtue: Vision Accessory: Custom Bike Cecelia: Level 83 (weapon) Goal: Use Time (armor) Community: Soulmates (armor) Virtue: Sorrow Accessory: Shard of Raw Efficiency Alayna: Level 83 (weapon) Goal: Find Self (armor) Community: Discussion Group (armor) Virtue: Self-Sufficiency Accessory: Feather of Stats Lisa: Level 83 (weapon) Goal: Analyze Books (armor) Community: Financial Independents (armor) Virtue: Self-Awareness Accessory: Letter of Resignation In closing..... whew, I'm tired of all the typing. I'll just say if you enjoy RPGs, definitely give this a try. And I bet those who haven't played many RPGs or aren't super fond of them might find a lot to love about this game regardless. Happy debt slaying!

text: There is a lot to like about this game. It is only minimally linear. There are several things you can do and only a few of them are required. However, the game is missing some very basic things that would make it so much better. First, a propper help screen would be nice. They don't do a great job explaining what does what so many combats end up being trial and error. Second, there isn't a settings screen, so I can't lower the music or sound effects, shame too since this is the kind of game I can play while listening to a podcast. Third, can't resize the screen in order to read things better. Still, does not mean the game is bad. It is fun and enjoyable and there was some clear thought put into it, which is why it is baffling that these basic features are not included.

title: Cubicle Quest
text: I'm someone who loves old fashioned JRPGs, but has gotten really bored with a lot of the RPG maker games on Steam.  I *really* like this game.  It's not without flaws, but a very fun experience.  The question you have to ask yourself is "am I okay with a game that is a big self-referential allegory?"  You arm yourself with goals, and armor yourself with a community of friends.  Enemies are life challenges.  In this game you will fight a succubus sprite labeled as "empty relationship", you will arm yourself with your goal of "read more books", and defend yourself with "drinking buddies".  if this bothers you, this is not the game for you. Short version: 8.5/10 strongly recommend to anyone who likes turn based JRPGs, and wasn't completely turned of by the premise. Interestingly many of the games strengths are also its weaknesses: Pros/Cons: + The battle system is interesting, but manages to not be as tedious as a lot of games that add extra random battles to pad game length.  Characters are largely not customizable, but the fact that you get a fairly large number means your party *is*.  Skills are varried enough that you have meaningful decisions in combat. - As with any turn-based JRPG type game, sometimes you're just hitting "attack" very quickly to kill weak enemies. -The game's allegorical nature sometimes makes things confusing.  I never had problems in other games making the connection that "lava breath" was a fire attack, but with attack types like "stress" and "laziness" it can sometimes be hard to pick out what attacks are doing, and the game isn't terrible forthcoming with the information + Music and sound is pretty generic, but very enjoyable.  I often mute games and play music, but I didn't for this one + I rather like the story, but I could see some people just not really "getting" it + A fun collection of characters to meet. - All the characters are pretty one dimensional.  Making friends, offering emotional support, and forming relationships are all core concepts to this game, so I feel like it could have used some more robust characters.  This isn't mass effect/Lornen/Dragon age + A surprisingly open world (gated somewhat like a metroidvania), that lets you figure out where you want to go and what you want to do. - Sometimes it's very hard to figure out what to do.  For instance when you start the game you're in debt, and you need to find a room mate and get a promotion at work.  What the game doesn't tell you is that the dungeon of promotion is basically impossible with a 1-man party, so you need to do them specifically in the room mate-> promotion order, unless you spend an hour or two grinding on the world map - There's also one or two areas I had trouble accessing.  Fortunately since the game is so open I didn't *need* to get into them, but it was still frustrating.

title: DARK
text: I really don't understand why, as of this date, the game has a 46%. It was a great game in many ways. The acting was supurb, the art was unique and fun, and the game play was good too. Often lower rated games crash but this one never crashed in the many times I alt tabbed and was competely stabe. I would guess the lack of an open world was a reason it didn't score well, but open worlds aren't always necessary. Retracing through the same city scape for no real reason woudn't have added much to the game. Now, I can see the benefits of being a vampire in a city and trying to find your way-- but tht would have been a completely different storyline. So yes, the game is on rails but the rails of these levels are nicely done and full of little things that doesn't make it feel that way. One thing the game could do better is its combat system. It reminded me of Styx or the first Assassin's Creed game in that sense. You really just got one attack- they should add more. Punching someone in the side of the head doesn't feel like you're killing them but I suppose you are. Had this game came out in 2006 - 2009 it probably would have scored in the high 80s but the combat felt clunky. The music in the Santuary dance hall was a bit repetitive. Some freeware beats would have worked inbetween the theme song. With all that said, you don't play a sneaking game only for combat- you play it for sneaking. And I thought this game did a great job with that. Guards investigated sounds, became alarm at bodies, talked about their fellow man who you slew in earlier levels. Radio broadcasts tie you to the events of the outside world. It really was immersive. It's too bad this game scores so low cause a sequel would be fun. At the end you get to choose one of two endings, I chose the one that isn't revenge so I'd like to get that revenge sometime. I haven't done the DLC yet, maybe there's some loose ends to tie up in that.

title: DARK
text: There are different kinds of stealth games. There's the gentle stealth game, like those mini stealth runs in LoZ that require no challenge at all. Then there's Skyrim stealth, which is ludicrous and meh. Then there's Dishonored stealth, where enemies actually react and show off how a person reacts to stealth, and pay attention to things. And then there's DARK. This game's stealth is INCREDIBLY difficult! And enjoyable. DARK is a challenging stealth game, putting you into the role of a vampire (you do not sparkle) trying to find his creator so he doesn't end up a mindless ghoul. The AI is well done; they follow good pathways and block exits normally, and during hostile moments they wander, and work well together. They cover each other. THEY GIVE COVER! Overall, worth the buy, but only if you enjoy stealth games. Otherwise, you'll spend hours just sitting in the same spot going "ffs move you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ guard."

text: Okay, so this game isn't as terrible as many reviewers have tried to paint it to be. That said, its not that good either. Everything this game tries to do, from atmosphere and graphics on down, Vampire the Masquerade: Bloodlines did 500% better ten years earlier. Frustrating? Yes. Horrible Voice Actor for the main character? Gods yes. Stiff animations? Yes. Clunky controls? Yes. Laughable AI? Most definitely. But past that there is still fun to be had here. The story isn't overly original thus far, and uses as many classic Vampire tropes as it can wedge in, but its just interesting enough to make it worth playing. I'd never suggest anyone paying the full $15 for it, there is just not enough good about it to warrant that price. I could see spending $5 or less on it if you're looking for something new to kill time on and enjoy a plot. Honestly I would suggest flipping it on easy, looking up a cheat program and just playing for the story, otherwise this game will likely make you want to put your fist through your monitor and sue Kalypso for having lost sanity and IQ points permanently to the flaws.
